title: BigQuery ObjectRef now GA: Build multimodal data platforms for conversational analytics entirely in SQL
raw_text:
For data science, data engineering, and machine learning teams, unlocking the value of unstructured data, such as images, videos, audio, and documents, has historically meant managing siloed data pipelines for structured and unstructured data, and for analytics and AI/ML use cases. Even when files remain in Cloud Storage, running inference requires teams to orchestrate external machine learning workloads, only to face the complex, brittle challenge of stitching those structured inference outputs back into the data warehouse for analysis. This post-hoc data-stitching introduces significant operational overhead and database misalignment. ObjectRef and multimodal data analytics in BigQuery are now in General Availability (GA) , establishing BigQuery as a comprehensive, multimodal agentic data platform. With ObjectRef, BigQuery natively bridges the gap between Cloud Storage and your analytical engine. You can represent unstructured data as native ObjectRef columns directly alongside your traditional relational columns. This unlocks a massive advantage over standalone model APIs by enabling you to pass multimodal, multi-column inputs directly to Gemini models in a single SQL query or natural language query using conversational analytics. ObjectRef integrations with BigQuery AI, conversational analytics in BigQuery and Gemini Enterprise enable you to easily combine Cloud Storage files with rich, structured database context, metadata, timestamps and custom agent instructions. You can now leverage BigQuery's core strengths (fully serverless compute, low total cost of ownership, and built-in at-scale inference) to build, run, and govern powerful unstructured-to-structured, unstructured-to-unstructured and fully multimodal-to-multimodal pipelines without separate compute clusters. Crucially, the extracted features and annotations can be combined directly with the unstructured object itself by storing the ObjectRef in the same row. Using this combined data directly in conversational analytics and AI agents avoids the loss of nuanced data and context that typically occurs when customers transform unstructured files into purely structured formats. Customers are already using this approach to generate embeddings for multimodal vector search , perform at-scale classification using GenAI , and execute precise data and feature extraction from vast archives of documents and media, all via standard SQL. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'SELECT
AI.AGG(image_ref, "Summarize the major categories of pictures")
FROM
`bigquery-public-data.cymbal_pets.products`;'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fbb9af08910>)])]> ObjectRef brings structure to the unstructured ObjectRef is a built-in, predefined STRUCT data type that points to objects outside of BigQuery. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', '-- ObjectRef is a special STRUCT in BigQuery 
struct {
 uri string,
 authorizer string,
 version string, 
 details json { 
	gcs_metadata json
 }
 }'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fbb9af09010>)])]> By storing these pointers natively in standard BigQuery tables alongside traditional columns, BigQuery treats unstructured files as first-class data citizens. Furthermore, this architecture supports independent data lifecycles: your GCS data and BigQuery tables can change independently without affecting the underlying data in the other system. This approach serves multiple data personas by offering powerful advantages: Zero-copy architecture: Keep your high-volume media files securely in Cloud Storage and query them instantly in BigQuery, respecting data gravity and avoiding costly data duplication. SQL and Python interoperability: You can query unstructured data using standard SQL or BigQuery DataFrames. Crucially, you can pass ObjectRefs into BigQuery Python UDFs, allowing you to bring open-source Python libraries, like OpenCV, directly to your data to execute custom logic without moving it. Independent lifecycles and versioning: ObjectRefs ensure reproducible inference by tracking specific GCS generation numbers. If the underlying GCS file changes, your query can still reference the exact version of the file that existed when the row was written. Unified governance: You can secure, audit, and share access to both structured columns and their related unstructured files using BigQuery's existing security policies and IAM controls. Create full-fidelity ETL with SQL Since launching ObjectRef in preview, a powerful, highly effective pattern has emerged among our users: building full-fidelity ETL pipelines entirely with SQL. Teams are leveraging BigQuery’s serverless architecture to integrate AI/ML directly into their data environments, eliminating the need for separate compute clusters to handle data movement and inference. Managing unstructured data in GCS as standard BigQuery columns allows users to apply core data engineering best practices, such as building idempotent pipelines, ensuring reproducibility, and executing seamless backfills, directly to images, video, audio, and documents. Once data is robustly prepared, teams use Gemini within BigQuery to execute full-fidelity ETL. They unlock dual-layer analytics by extracting features and annotating unstructured data while keeping the original ObjectRef anchored in the same row. The structured outputs power fast filtering, reporting and BI dashboards, while the attached unstructured objects remain available for deep, context-heavy reasoning. For example, you might extract sentiment scores and topic tags from an archive of customer call recordings to quickly flag at-risk accounts on a BI dashboard (the structured layer). Simultaneously, a conversational analytics agent evaluating escalation processes can seamlessly fall back to the original audio files to analyze the caller and customer service representative interactions, preventing the loss of critical nuance that typically occurs in unstructured-to-structured ETL pipelines. Proven use cases from industry leaders “At Snap, the safety of our community is a top priority, and we aim to limit users’ exposure to content that violates our Community Guidelines. We regularly review samples of public posts, and by leveraging ObjectRef with BigQuery AI, we transitioned from simple random sampling to post-stratification sampling. This transition improved the efficiency of our human review processes, enabling us to reinvest reclaimed capacity into new and expanded workflows that further enhance our ability to detect and address potentially harmful content.” - Carlos Ortiz , Data Scientist, Snap During the preview phase, we saw adoption across a variety of critical workloads. Customers have successfully transitioned these experimental pipelines into production, transforming unstructured data into actionable, structured insights: Content moderation: Online platforms leverage BigQuery to integrate multimedia assets with standard telemetry data in a single pipeline to fundamentally enhance their moderation and safety outcomes. Proactive threat detection: Enterprise security teams use BigQuery to analyze visual and structural web components alongside network logs, driving critical advancements in proactive threat identification. Inventory compliance: Online retailers extract text and context directly from vast image repositories to automatically flag regulatory or brand compliance issues at scale. Customer experience: Service-oriented enterprises analyze audio interactions between support agents and customers with BigQuery AI to evaluate customer sentiment and improve service delivery. New in GA We streamlined the developer experience for the General Availability release, focusing on support for a wide variety of customer use cases: Flexible authentication: In GA, we introduced End User Credentials (EUC) support for ObjectRefs . Users can now quickly query and explore unstructured data using their personal IAM identity directly for ad-hoc analysis. In preview, querying unstructured files required setting up explicit BigQuery connections for ObjectRefs . While these connections remain fully supported and are the recommended best practice for robust, service-account-driven production pipelines , we recognize they require additional setup. Unified support for your Cloud Storage metadata: We know your unstructured data’s metadata lives in various places across Google Cloud. ObjectRef now natively supports the full spectrum of these sources. Whether your metadata currently resides in BigQuery object tables , Cloud Storage insights datasets , or simply as raw string URIs within standard BigQuery tables, you can seamlessly create and manage ObjectRefs to analyze the underlying data. Array support for comparative analytics: We introduced native support for processing ObjectRefs contained within arrays. This enables entirely new classes of workloads, such as comparing multiple documents against one another, analyzing sequences of images, or batching items in a single semantic call. See it in action: End-to-end multimodal analytics To illustrate the power of these GA updates, let's look at how you can build real-world, multimodal pipelines using our streamlined SQL operators. 1. Full-fidelity ETL: Call center audio analysis Analyzing customer service calls historically required moving audio files to specialized transcription and natural language processing clusters. With ObjectRef , you can parse audio files, extract structured business intelligence and add them directly as standard relational columns. Use the GA OBJ.MAKE_REF() function to automatically detect the audio format from a raw string URI and BigQuery’s managed AI functions for well known use-cases. For example, you can use AI.CLASSIFY() to categorize customer call types. By default, BigQuery uses Optimized Mode for AI Functions to reduce the number of tokens consumed. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE call_center.annotated_call_logs AS
SELECT 
 customer_id,
 call_date,
 OBJ.MAKE_REF(audio_uri) as ref,
 AI.CLASSIFY(
 OBJ.MAKE_REF(audio_uri), [
 "Lost or stolen card", 
 "Declined card payment", 
 "Activate my card",
 "Order physical card",
 "Cancel transfer",
 "Password or pin forgotten",
 "Virtual card not working",
 "Card swallowed by ATM",
 "Balance not updated after bank transfer",
 "Balance not updated after check or cash deposit",
 "Extra charge on statement",
 "Transfer fee charged"
 ]
 ) AS customer_issue_type,
 FROM 
 call_center.raw_call_logs;'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fbb9af098d0>)])]> This table can serve as a multimodal data source for a BigQuery conversational analytics agent. The agent translates natural language queries into SQL using BigQuery AI functions to analyze audio files when additional information is needed. 2. At-scale gen AI filtering: Product compliance Data engineers frequently need to filter massive datasets based on the contents of images or documents. Instead of running heavy generative queries and parsing text outputs, you can now use the declarative AI.IF() operator natively alongside your standard SQL in WHERE clauses. The default Optimized Mode reduces the number of tokens consumed to further optimize your workloads. code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'SELECT 
 product_id,
 seller_id,
FROM 
 ecommerce.vendor_uploads
WHERE 
 upload_date >= CURRENT_DATE() - 1 AND
 AI.IF(("Does this product image contain a restricted item or policy violation?", OBJ.MAKE_REF(image_uri))'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fbb99be09d0>)])]> 3. Multi-object reasoning: Proactive threat detection With native array support in GA, you can now pass an array of ObjectRefs into a single Gemini call to analyze multiple files simultaneously using Gemini. This unlocks complex comparative logic directly in SQL. For example, a security team can pass a screenshot of their official login page and a screenshot of a newly discovered, suspicious webpage to Gemini simultaneously to detect phishing attempts at scale: code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'SELECT 
 log_id,
 suspect_domain,
 assessment.is_phishing,
 assessment.visual_discrepancies
FROM (
 SELECT 
 log_id,
 suspect_domain,
 AI.GENERATE(
 (
 "Compare these two web UI screenshots. The first is our official, trusted login page. The second is a suspected spoofed page. Identify any visual discrepancies, missing logos, or fake elements, and determine if it is a phishing attempt.", 
 [OBJ.MAKE_REF(trusted_ui_uri),OBJ.MAKE_REF(suspect_ui_uri)]
 ),
 output_schema => 'is_phishing BOOLEAN, visual_discrepancies STRING'
 ) AS assessment
 FROM 
 cybersecurity.network_ui_logs
);'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fbb9b02c410>)])]> Start analyzing today BigQuery ObjectRef is now generally available on all BigQuery editions and on-demand pricing tiers. If you are currently managing complex, fragmented infrastructure just to perform machine learning inference on your Cloud Storage files, it's time to consolidate. Bring AI directly to your storage. Start leveraging your existing data engineering practices to build robust, scalable, and secure multimodal analytics pipelines directly within BigQuery. To get started with ObjectRef and multimodal analytics, check out these resources: Walk through our hands-on tutorial to generate image captions and assign product categories using synthetic data. Watch live demos from Cloud Next about unifying unstructured and structured data , and generating text with LLMs and performing vector search . Learn how to work with ObjectRef in the BigQuery documentation.
summary: For data science, data engineering, and machine learning teams, unlocking the value of unstructured data, such as images, videos, audio, and documents, has historically meant managing siloed data pipelines for structured and unstructured data, and for analytics and AI/ML use cases. Even when files remain in Cloud Storage, running inference requires teams to orchestrate external machine learning workloads, only to face the complex, brittle challenge of stitching those structured inference outputs back into the data warehouse for analysis. This post-hoc data-stitching introduces significant operational overhead and database misalignment. ObjectRef and multimodal data analytics in BigQuery are now in General Availability (GA) , establishing BigQuery as a comprehensive, multimodal agentic data platform.

title: ZenteiQ scales batch inference 4x with GKE Inference Gateway powered by llm-d
raw_text: Today we hear from ZenteiQ , an artificial intelligence startup spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) and selected under the IndiaAI Mission to build sovereign scientific foundation models from the ground up. To pre-train models that understand physical laws, governing equations, and numerical solvers, ZenteiQ designed and built a large-scale batch synthetic data-generation pipeline that runs across multiple model families and feeds verified datasets into training runs. Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and GKE Inference Gateway gave ZenteiQ the inference-routing layer within its pipeline to scale aggregate inference throughput 4.07x and grow daily output from 1.47 billion to 5.97 billion generated tokens for every 1,000 accelerators. - Fisayo Feyisetan, Product Manager, Google Cloud Unlike general-purpose language models trained primarily on web text and code, scientific foundation models must understand complex physical systems, mathematical governing equations, and numerical solvers across domains such as thermodynamics, computational fluid dynamics, and electromagnetics. At ZenteiQ, we are building sovereign scientific foundation models from scratch that interpret simulation outputs, evaluate equation formulations, and work through step-by-step mathematical derivations that obey physical laws. Pre-training models on large datasets of governing equations takes hundreds of billions of reasoning tokens. Alongside curated scientific literature and simulation datasets, we also rely on a batch synthetic data-generation pipeline that we independently designed and implemented to generate, evaluate, and filter candidate derivations and solver validation problems before feeding them into our MaxText pre-training jobs. Because we operate on a fixed compute allocation, every hour our accelerators spend generating and verifying training data is an hour taken away from pre-training. When data generation falls behind, multi-host accelerator clusters reserved for pre-training sit idle, waiting on datasets. When data generation slows down pre-training To maximize data generation speed, our pipeline separates prompt preparation on worker pods from model serving on vLLM across multi-node accelerator pools. Each batch moves through four stages: expanding scientific seed concepts into prompt batches, generating candidate reasoning traces with generator models, scoring responses using evaluator models, and running guardrail checks with a separate model family before packaging verified datasets for pre-training. We originally ran these model pools on Kubernetes with standard ClusterIP round-robin load balancing across inference endpoints. As we scaled our pipeline to feed our 9B- and 35B-parameter model schedules, two routing bottlenecks began slowing down dataset creation. Uneven engine queues: Our upstream worker pods expand seed concepts into prompts of widely varying complexity and response length. Because standard round-robin load balancing had no visibility into vLLM engine queues, it kept sending new requests to serving pods that were already busy processing long reasoning traces, while neighboring nodes had capacity to spare. Redundant prefix computation: Prompts within a generation batch share roughly 70% to 80% of their instructional context and task specifications. Round-robin routing scattered requests with identical instructions across different serving instances, forcing each pod to recompute the same shared prompt prefix from scratch instead of reusing warm caches in accelerator memory. Together, uneven queues and redundant prefill work caused our generation throughput to swing by as much as half within a single run, stretching out dataset creation and delaying the start of scheduled pre-training runs. We needed routing that understood live vLLM queue depths and prompt caches, without pulling our researchers off model development to build and maintain a custom inference scheduler. Building on GKE Inference Gateway powered by llm-d We already run our data preparation and MaxText pre-training jobs on GKE, which lets our team manage data generation and model training on the same Kubernetes platform. Following a recommendation from Google Cloud to address our routing bottlenecks without changing our underlying scientific methodology or pipeline design, we deployed GKE Inference Gateway , powered by the open-source llm-d distributed inference framework, in front of our vLLM accelerator pools. In our pipeline, worker pods pull scientific seed documents and domain taxonomies from Cloud Storage and expand them into batches of multi-step prompts. Those batches flow through a single GKE Inference Gateway deployment that manages traffic across all of our model families and serving nodes. Rather than maintaining isolated routing for each model tier, we route generation requests, evaluation queries, and guardrail checks across their respective model pools through the same gateway. Once candidate responses pass evaluation and guardrail checks, worker pods deduplicate and package the verified datasets for direct consumption by downstream MaxText pre-training jobs on GKE. GKE Inference Gateway routes batch generation, evaluation, and guardrail requests across multi-node accelerator pools running vLLM before verified datasets are fed into MaxText pre-training. From round-robin to load- and cache-aware routing With GKE Inference Gateway and llm-d, routing decisions use live serving signals from our vLLM instances rather than static round-robin rotation. GKE Inference Gateway continuously monitors real-time queue depth and key-value (KV) cache utilization across our vLLM endpoints. When a serving node is busy decoding a long equation derivation, the gateway routes incoming requests to nodes with open capacity, so heavy prompts no longer pile up behind busy workers while neighboring nodes sit idle. At the same time, the gateway routes requests with matching scientific instructions to the serving node where that prefix’s KV cache is already warm in accelerator memory. Because 70% to 80% of each prompt is shared instructional context while the generated reasoning trajectories vary from request to request, combining prefix-cache locality with live queue balancing lets our pods skip repeated prefill work without overloading any single replica. Higher throughput, predictable training runs Adopting GKE Inference Gateway powered by llm-d transformed the speed and predictability of our data generation pipeline. Across our production clusters, intelligent routing delivered: 4x higher fleet throughput: Aggregate throughput jumped from 16,964 to 69,114 tokens per second per 1,000 accelerators — growing daily output from 1.47 billion to nearly 6 billion generated tokens . 3.5x to 5.5x gains across individual model pools: Real-time queue balancing kept serving nodes evenly loaded throughout each run, preventing the mid-run slowdowns caused by long reasoning derivations. 14-percentage-point higher prefix-cache hit rate: Routing prompts with matching scientific instructions to warm caches avoided redundant prefill work before each request branched into its own derivation. For our research and infrastructure teams, the most important outcome was schedule predictability. Quadrupling daily output meant verified datasets were ready on time, so our multi-host pre-training runs started on schedule instead of waiting on data generation. What’s next for physical AI at ZenteiQ As we scale our scientific foundation models from 9B to 35B parameters and beyond, we plan to use the same GKE Inference Gateway and llm-d routing setup for post-training reinforcement learning (RL) and automated numerical solver evaluation loops. Because each turn in those multi-turn rollouts builds on the context of the turns before it, they depend even more heavily on live queue balancing and warm prefix caches. To try these capabilities on your own workloads, explore the GKE Inference Gateway documentation and check out the open-source llm-d project . You can also read how the Gemini platform team cut latency by 35% with GKE Inference Gateway .
summary: Today we hear from ZenteiQ , an artificial intelligence startup spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) and selected under the IndiaAI Mission to build sovereign scientific foundation models from the ground up. To pre-train models that understand physical laws, governing equations, and numerical solvers, ZenteiQ designed and built a large-scale batch synthetic data-generation pipeline that runs across multiple model families and feeds verified datasets into training runs. Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and GKE Inference Gateway gave ZenteiQ the inference-routing layer within its pipeline to scale aggregate inference throughput 4.07x and grow daily output from 1.47 billion to 5.97 billion generated tokens for every 1,000 accelerators. - Fisayo Feyisetan, Product Manager, Google Cloud Unlike general-purpose language models trained primarily on web text and code, scientific foundation models must understand complex physical systems, mathematical governing equations, and numerical solvers across domains such as thermodynamics, computational fluid dynamics, and electromagnetics.

title: Responding to core PHP vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
raw_text: Editor's note : This blog was updated on Oct. 21, 2026 at 3:30 p.m. PDT with additional guidance on Cloud Armor, and at 4:25 p.m. PDT with additional guidance on monitoring, patching, and remediation. PHP and Wiz Research disclosed today two critical vulnerabilities in the core PHP language runtime that can expose applications to unauthenticated remote code execution and memory disclosure. Wiz used a mix of models to identify and help remediate these vulnerabilities. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch. While Google Cloud itself is not vulnerable, users of PHP running on Google Cloud may be vulnerable . At Google Cloud, we understand the severity of these vulnerabilities, and are sharing guidance to help our customers take immediate action to secure their applications. Vulnerability background PHP is a widely-used, server-side scripting language that powers many websites, content management systems, and web applications. On Oct. 21, 2026, CVE.org assigned the vulnerabilities as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The official Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base severity score for each of the PHP flaws has been determined as Critical, a severity of 9.2. Generally, this ranking means that threat actors can crash and hijack the affected system, and can easily steal, alter, and wipe its data — although mitigating circumstances can make it harder to exploit the flaw. CVE-2026-109618 : Out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 : Request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. Vulnerable versions : All versions of PHP from 5.4 through 8.5.11 Patched in : PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 Not patched : The PHP project is not releasing fixes for PHP 8.1 or earlier, which have reached end of life . Fix : CVE-2026-109618 ( GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w ) and CVE-2026-109619 ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ): Announcement : PHP has published a security advisory on these two vulnerabilities. Wiz Research has published a detailed description of the research and the coordinated disclosure process. Update PHP and redeploy your applications We urge all customers running PHP applications on Google Cloud to immediately update to PHP 8.2 or newer, and redeploy their services using a patched version. This applies specifically to applications deployed on: App Engine standard environment : Supported runtimes are patched automatically. If you are on PHP 8.1 or earlier, upgrade to PHP 8.2 or newer and redeploy. App Engine flexible environment : Redeploy your PHP runtimes using a supported runtime. If you are using a custom runtime, update your PHP dependencies to a patched version and redeploy your application. Cloud Run : If automatic base image updates are not enabled, or you deploy your own container image, rebuild with a patched version of PHP and redeploy. Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) : Update your container images with a patched version of PHP and redeploy your pods. Google Cloud Marketplace : If you run a Marketplace solution that includes PHP, such as a content management system or LAMP stack, apply the update from the solution provider or update PHP directly. Automatic patches for serverless platforms Google Cloud is rolling out updated serverless base images for all supported PHP versions on App Engine Standard, App Engine Flexible, Cloud Run, Cloud Run function, and Cloud Functions for Firebase. What this means for you: App Engine standard environment (PHP 8.2 and newer): Applications are updated automatically. No action is required. App Engine flexible environment (all PHP versions): Applications are not updated automatically. Redeploy your application as soon as possible to PHP 8.2 and newer. Cloud Run functions (PHP 8.2 and newer): Functions with automatic base image updates enabled are updated automatically. Functions without automatic base image updates enabled must be redeployed. Cloud Run (PHP 8.2 and newer): Services with automatic base image updates enabled are updated automatically. Services built without automatic base image updates must be rebuilt and redeployed to pick up the patched runtime. Important considerations: Unsupported runtimes will not be patched . The upstream PHP project is not backporting these fixes to PHP 8.1 or earlier. Applications on PHP 5.5, PHP 7.2, PHP 7.3, PHP 7.4, or PHP 8.1 remain vulnerable and must be upgraded to PHP 8.2 or newer. See the following runtime support schedules for serverless lifecycle dates: Google App Engine Standard Google App Engine Flexible Cloud Run Cloud Run functions Container images you build yourself are your responsibility . If you have deployed your own container image to Cloud Run or App Engine Flexible (such as with a custom runtime), rebuild it with a patched version of PHP and redeploy. Mitigating CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 with Cloud Armor Cloud Armor has issued recommended mitigations that use Cloud Armor managed rules . Customers with active managed rules do not need to take action; protection against these vulnerabilities is applied automatically. If you have not yet deployed Cloud Armor managed rules, doing so now can still help you mitigate these vulnerabilities. The Cloud Armor managed rules protections are available now through automatically-updated threat intelligence rulesets. These rules are intended to help protect your internet-facing PHP applications and services that use global or regional application load balancers. Follow these steps to deploy the rules immediately as a frontline defense-in-depth mitigation while your vulnerability management program updates and verifies all vulnerable PHP instances in your environment. 1. Deploying canary and stable managed rules (preview and enforce mode) for automatic updates: In order to protect your workloads from these CVEs, customers should minimally enable the File Upload and RFI categories . We recommend that you configure all ruleset categories in the canary version in preview mode, and ruleset categories in the stable version in enforced mode. 2. Mitigate risk on request bodies that exceed configured inspection limits: Create a rule in your security policies to help ensure that no uninspected or unnecessarily large content reaches your backends. This is particularly important for these CVEs, which may use large payloads to trigger out-of-memory conditions. Verifying WAF rule safety for your application and consuming telemetry Because PHP applications and content-management platforms (such as WordPress and Drupal) vary widely in how they structure query parameters, form submissions, and custom error handlers, we strongly recommend deploying the rules described above in preview mode first so you can test and monitor the expected impact without actively blocking traffic. Once you’ve verified that the new rule is behaving as expected for your application traffic, disable preview mode to allow Cloud Armor to actively enforce the deny(403) action. Cloud Armor per-request web application firewall (WAF) telemetry is emitted as part of the application load balancer logs in Cloud Logging. To inspect Cloud Armor's decision on every request load balancer request logging first needs to be enabled on a per-backend-service basis . Once enabled, all subsequent Cloud Armor enforcement and preview decisions can be queried in Cloud Logging by following these instructions . We recommend consulting our Cloud Armor best practices guide and accounting for service limitations (such as maximum inspected request body sizes, covered above) to minimize risk and optimize performance. Monitoring and auditing Google Cloud and Wiz are currently supporting customers with active monitoring, auditing, and runtime detection across its native security offerings. Customers can use: On-Demand Scanning AP I to manually scan images stored locally on your computer or remotely in Artifact Registry. Customers using Artifact Analysis will be notified of these vulnerabilities on both new and existing artifacts to identify at-risk workloads. Security Command Center to enable container threat detection for GKE and Cloud Run threat detection to monitor their workloads for intrusions. Google Security Operations now has 23 new curated detections added to the Mandiant Frontline Threats rule pack. We recommend verifying that this rule pack is enabled and reviewing your detections to assess any potential impact to your environment. Enterprise Plus customers can additionally use the Emerging Threat Center and search for “GLOBAL.26.015” for further details. Enterprise plus customers who have enabled the Threat Hunt Agent in Public Preview can also perform a hunt on GLOBAL.26.015 from the Emerging Threats Center. Wiz customers can refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell, which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance. More information is available here on response steps with Wiz. Additionally, Mandiant Threat Defense is actively supporting customers by monitoring curated detections in Google Security Operations and hunting for evidence of intrusion activity related to this campaign. Patching and remediation The PHP security release has been published. You should update PHP across every server environment, container image, and deployment pipeline. In addition: As part of Wiz's zero-day response commitment, WizOS PHP images are available at zero billable units for all customers for the next 60 days. WizOS PHP base images, both standard Alpine-hardened and FIPS-compliant builds, are already patched against CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, built from source. Wiz customers can use the Green Agent to translate the PHP2Shell Threat Intel advisory into resource-tailored remediation guidance, including prescribing the correct PHP patch versions, identifying the right WAF mitigations, recommending opportunities to swap in for hardened WizOS PHP images, and suggesting enabling runtime blocking where there are gaps. We will continue to monitor the situation closely and provide further updates and guidance as necessary. For the most current information and detailed steps, please refer to the Google Cloud security bulletin .
summary: Editor's note : This blog was updated on Oct. 21, 2026 at 3:30 p.m. PDT with additional guidance on Cloud Armor, and at 4:25 p.m. PDT with additional guidance on monitoring, patching, and remediation.

title: Google Public Sector increases partner investments for frontline adoption
raw_text: Partnership is at the core of Google Public Sector’s mission to empower government agencies and education institutions with transformative, mission-aligned solutions. We recognize that we can only scale our impact through a thriving, highly capable partner community. At today’s Partner Connect at Google Public Sector Summit , we are introducing enhanced partner initiatives focused on fostering deeper collaboration, supercharging frontline adoption, and expanding mission delivery capabilities across our valued partner network. These updates are centered around four pillars: Enhanced partner incentives: We will reward partners who do the heavy lifting of pre-sales technical depth, solution design, and proof-of-concept execution through newly announced incentives and discounts. Partner-Led User Success Program: We will support sustained frontline Gemini adoption led by our partners through three targeted investments. Training and enablement: Launching a new Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) academy, a rigorous bootcamp designed to build elite, Google-trained FDEs inside partner’s practices. Pre-sales acceleration: Increasing our Pre-Sales Deal Acceleration Funds to directly co-invest in partner-led customer workshops and proofs of concept. Post-sales adoption: Expanding our investment pool to $45M in dedicated deployment and adoption funding , designed to pay for partner professional services to deploy Gemini across the entirety of the U.S. public sector for the first time—ensuring day-one operational readiness. Backing builders and powering alliances: We know specialized missions require purpose-built software and scalable infrastructure. We are launching a new ISV Agent Factory to accelerate the development of specialized public sector agents. This is on top of our ISV ATO Accelerator which provides individual ISVs up to $1M in funding from Google to offset the cost of GovRAMP, FedRAMP, and DoD Impact Level accreditations. Market-accelerating alliances: We are announcing a new Strategic Alliance with SHI to activate 400+ sellers across state, local, and education markets. At the federal level, Accenture Federal Services is announcing new Gemini Launchpads to help agencies move from agentic experimentation to mission execution, faster. In the public sector, technology is never just about deployment; it is about the mission. Together with our partners, we are ensuring that our joint public sector customers have the mission-ready capabilities they need to lead on the front lines. To operationalize these announcements, partner organizations are encouraged to engage in the programs below and access upcoming trainings: Google Public Sector Partner Enablement Series Google Public Sector Partner Specialty Badge Program ISV ATO Accelerator

title: Google Cloud expands model choice and flexibility, bringing OpenAI models to customers
raw_text: Google Cloud has always been defined by choice, enterprise-grade governance, and market-leading price-performance. Key to the foundation of openness and choice is giving customers flexibility to run agentic workloads across their choice of models and infrastructure to achieve the right balance of cost, capability, and performance. Today, we are expanding that foundation by launching OpenAI models in Google Cloud’s model garden. Google Cloud is now the only hyperscale cloud provider offering access to all three leading closed source LLMs, alongside more than 200 first-party, third-party, and open models on a unified enterprise AI platform. The right model for every workload Modern enterprise AI requires matching each workload to the right model rather than relying on a single model for every task. By adding OpenAI’s newest models to model garden, we are giving teams options across the full spectrum of enterprise workloads. For OpenAI models: GPT-6 Astra : Designed for demanding work across coding, computer use, professional tasks, and scientific research. GPT-6.1 Sol : Near-Astra intelligence at lower cost across agentic coding, computer use, and professional work. GPT-6 Luna : A fast, cost-efficient model for everyday work at scale. Using the platform, customers can dynamically select and swap the optimal model for any use case based on performance, latency, and cost efficiency without architectural lock-in or separate vendor contracts. Developers gain the freedom to build with hundreds of choices in model garden. Because OpenAI models are transacted directly through Google Cloud Marketplace, all usage appears on a single Google Cloud invoice, draws down existing cloud commitments, and counts toward Flexible Savings Plans (FSP) across model providers. Built-in data governance and enterprise security Scaling generative AI should never require compromising on compliance or security. Built from the ground up for enterprise governance, the Gemini platform is trusted by leading global organizations today. We ensure that running any third-party or OpenAI workload meets the most rigorous enterprise standards: Strict data perimeters : Customer prompts, context, and outputs remain entirely within your designated data perimeter and are never used to train foundation models, with Zero Data Retention (ZDR) options available coming soon. Isolated access boundaries : OpenAI models run on dedicated Google Cloud infrastructure with Confidential Compute coming soon. All queries are routed through hardened, isolated gateways, ensuring data transit remains strictly within Google Cloud's secure environment and third-party model providers have no unauthorized access to your cloud environment. Unified auditing and identity : Every agent and model interaction operates under an authenticated identity, giving IT administrators end-to-end visibility, VPC Service Controls protection, and unified audit logging across their entire enterprise footprint. “Helping customers put AI to work across their enterprise content requires leading models backed by strong security and rigorous compliance standards,” said Yashodha Bhavnani, VP of AI Products at Box. “By using OpenAI models through Google Cloud, we will be able to give customers access to OpenAI’s frontier AI models alongside Google Cloud’s security and compliance capabilities, enabling them to get more value from their enterprise content. This is a step toward operating more efficiently as we bring AI to customers.” Getting started OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna models are rolling out now in private preview to select enterprise customers in Google Cloud’s model garden, with more coming soon. Starting today, customers can build with these models through our APIs and connect their local Codex CLI and Desktop workflows directly to our Gemini platform for inference. Please use this form to express interest. Coming soon, OpenAI models will be available in Google Cloud’s Gemini for business and Google Antigravity, providing enterprise customers and developers with model choice flexibility and the best model for each task.

Google Cloud is now the only hyperscale cloud provider offering access to all three leading closed source LLMs, alongside more than 200 first-party, third-party, and open models on a unified enterprise AI platform.

title: Hardware-backed security at global scale: Confidential G4 with NVIDIA Blackwell is GA
raw_text: Bringing autonomous agents into production means processing sensitive data and valuable intellectual property in real time. Protecting proprietary model weights, user prompts, and generated outputs requires security that safeguards data while it is actively being computed. As part of our efforts to enable your enterprise securely, today we are announcing that Confidential Computing on Google Cloud’s G4 instances enabled by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server edition GPUs is now generally available. This release integrates NVIDIA Confidential Computing directly into Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer , delivering the dynamic performance needed to scale without compromising privacy. When we announced Confidential G4 in preview earlier this year, we talked about its global footprint and scale. Today, these instances are generally available across 36 zones , using multiple consumption models , on Compute Engine VMs and GKE nodes . In addition, support for Confidential Space enabling secure multi-party data sharing is rolling out to general availability in the coming weeks. Protecting sensitive data and models at low latency Protecting data in use shouldn't mean sacrificing GPU throughput or operational agility. By combining non-exportable hardware keys, verifiable remote attestation, and transparent memory encryption, Confidential G4 helps organizations maximize their investments in agentic and inference workloads. Enterprises can keep costs low while meeting strict regulatory and compliance requirements. “As organizations deploy AI across increasingly complex cloud, on-premises, and agentic environments, protecting sensitive data is critical. Enterprises must also ensure that AI systems operate securely and consistently with their policies. Google Cloud Confidential G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs provide a powerful foundation for privacy-preserving AI and AI operations. Confidential Core AI builds on Google Cloud to transform enterprise principles, policies, and operating requirements into real-time safeguards that monitor and govern AI agents, models, data, and tools. Together, these capabilities enable organizations to scale trusted AI on Google Cloud while maintaining control, confidentiality, and accountability.” - Taher Behbehani, Founder and CEO, Confidential Core AI Additional benefits for enterprise AI workloads include: End-to-end confidentiality and isolation: Encrypt data and model parameters in hardware-enforced execution environments to shield intellectual property and customer inputs from host system administrators, hypervisors, and access by cloud providers. Verifiable cryptographic trust: Use hardware-rooted remote attestation to verify code, platform configuration, and environment integrity before releasing sensitive datasets and running workloads. No code refactoring: Deploy models out of the box using standard Ubuntu OS images, NVIDIA drivers, and NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries without application changes or custom builds. For Polaris Cloud, this ease of deployment was transformational. “Polaris builds workspaces for AI agents, and our customers need to know where an agent's work actually ran and that it was cryptographically isolated along the way. Google Cloud Confidential G4 has been a game changer for that. We get hardware-backed provenance from the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, which we bind into the receipt customers get back with their results. Virtually nothing else changed: same G4 image, same NVIDIA driver, same container runtime, one flag at launch, same performance. Overnight it upgraded our customer promise from 'we run your agent' to 'every workload you run with us is verifiable.” - Fred Esere, Founder and CEO, Polaris Cloud Multi-party data collaboration: Run collaborative analytics and joint model training securely using Confidential Space. Multiple parties can combine sensitive datasets without revealing underlying private data to each other. “Enterprises need to put their most valuable data to work with AI while protecting it during processing. NVIDIA Confidential Computing brings hardware-backed protection to GPU-accelerated workloads, helping safeguard sensitive data and proprietary models while in use. Together with Google Cloud, we’re bringing NVIDIA Blackwell performance and these security capabilities to Confidential G4 VMs so organizations can scale production AI with high performance and verifiable protection.” - Dave Salvator, Director of Accelerated Computing Products, NVIDIA Testing performance To understand the operational impact of memory encryption, we analyzed Confidential G4 instances against standard, non-confidential G4 instances on the g4-standard-48 machine shape. Our testing focused on widely adopted open-weight models that customers frequently deploy on single-GPU instances for their own inference pipelines. Benchmarking across popular models including Llama 3, Llama 3.3, Resnet-50, and SDXL shows that Confidential G4 delivers performance on par with standard G4 instances for AI inference workloads, with less than 3.5% degradation in throughput (measured in tokens or images per second). Note: Performance results are based on specific testing conditions and configurations. Individual workload performance may vary based on system setup, hardware choice, and software environment. Our analysis can help you move fast while protecting sensitive data and meeting compliance requirements — a trade-off that real-world deployments are already validating. ” We benchmarked Google Cloud's Confidential G4 against a standard G4 running identical software on our workloads . We found that for a modest 5.2% increase in end-to-end latency, we get a hardware-level assurance that ensures unauthorized users outside our users' attested environment cannot eavesdrop on their conversations. We'd make that trade every time; our users get the convenience of the cloud with the privacy of on-premises. ” - Andy Qin, CEO, Vertebrae Getting started with Confidential G4s With Confidential G4, improving enterprise security during model execution and agentic workloads doesn't require sacrificing performance, flexibility, or operational simplicity. By providing verifiable trust and robust hardware isolation with near-zero throughput degradation, organizations can securely deploy high-value models and protect critical data assets at cloud scale. Get started today by following the Confidential VM with GPU documentation .
summary: Bringing autonomous agents into production means processing sensitive data and valuable intellectual property in real time. Protecting proprietary model weights, user prompts, and generated outputs requires security that safeguards data while it is actively being computed. As part of our efforts to enable your enterprise securely, today we are announcing that Confidential Computing on Google Cloud’s G4 instances enabled by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server edition GPUs is now generally available. This release integrates NVIDIA Confidential Computing directly into Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer , delivering the dynamic performance needed to scale without compromising privacy.

title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA expand co-engineering collaboration to scale infrastructure for the agentic era
raw_text: As enterprises transition to continuous, multi-step agentic workflows, traditional infrastructure is hitting its limits. But raw performance is only part of the equation. To truly scale agentic AI, enterprises also need the flexibility to run the right models for the right tasks, alongside the data and operational sovereignty required to maintain verifiable control over both their sensitive intellectual property and the underlying infrastructure. Today at NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026, we are announcing new advancements across the stack to deliver this foundation: minimizing bottlenecks, expanding ecosystem choice, and introducing new sovereign AI and Confidential Computing capabilities to protect your most sensitive workloads with hardware-enforced security. Architecting for the agentic era To help you train, serve, and operate models at scale, Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer is built on compute, storage, networking, and software that we co-designed as a single system. Today, in collaboration with NVIDIA, we are announcing new updates to this agent-native infrastructure: Accelerated computing with A5X instances based on NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform : These bare-metal GPU-accelerated instances feature the latest NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform to deliver performance at scale. With general availability, coming next month, we are also expanding our infrastructure footprint to support EMEA data residency and sovereignty requirements with availability in new local regions. Scale-out A5X networking with Virgo Network: Virgo Network supports a non-blocking intra- and inter-building scale-out fabric via mesh topology. This new capability will enable extreme horizontal scaling, allowing clusters to expand to 80,000 Rubin GPUs within a single site and up to 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multi-site deployments. Storage with Managed Lustre and NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage: Google Cloud Managed Lustre will support NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage on A5X instances, giving training and inference data a direct RDMA path from the parallel file system into GPU memory, bypassing the CPU and system memory. Long-context memory with KV Caching: A5X instances will also support advanced KV-caching capabilities designed to scale context memory beyond GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for long-context and multi-turn agentic workloads. This high-speed caching layer will offload and reuse context across storage tiers, reducing redundant computation, lowering time-to-first-token, and improving inference goodput per dollar. Workload orchestration with A5X instances on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): GKE brings a suite of features for distributed AI workloads, such as GKE Managed DRANET , which simplifies RDMA management by making network interface cards first-class native Kubernetes resources; and Kueue , which boosts performance of distributed workloads through topology-aware scheduling and resource management. This makes GKE and A5X instances a powerful combination for agentic workload orchestration. “The true promise of agentic AI isn’t just speed, it’s freeing up human creativity from the friction of modern production pipelines. With Google Cloud’s A5X instances accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, our WPP Creative and Production teams can direct intelligent agents that perform frame-accurate quality checks and adapt brand assets seamlessly. Google Cloud gives us the reliability, scale and sovereign security required to meet our clients' most ambitious creative demands.” - Stephan Pretorius, Chief Technology Officer, WPP Expanding open models and ecosystem innovation Agentic workflows rarely rely on a single model. They route tasks to the most efficient model for the job. Your infrastructure should expand your options rather than restrict your roadmap. With Google Cloud, you can deploy infrastructure on your choice of software and NVIDIA AI infrastructure across multicloud, hybrid, and highly regulated environments. Today, we announced several updates to give you the freedom to build and adapt quickly: Open models: We are adding support for models like Gemma, Mistral, NVIDIA Nemotron, and others to our Sovereign Cloud portfolio . This allows you to run and govern open-weight models, while retaining full custody of model weights and runtimes, avoiding lock-in while maintaining high-performance acceleration. NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 SuperVL with NVIDIA NeMo now available on Gemini : You can now customize the new NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 SuperVL model with Managed Training Clusters . Use an MTC-optimized training recipe to jumpstart your Nemotron post-training work with NVIDIA NeMo RL and NVIDIA NeMo Gym on Google Cloud. With NVIDIA Cosmos 3, you can generate virtual worlds where robots and autonomous vehicles can try, fail and improve before real-world deployment, supporting simulation-to-reality workflows. Securing deployment with Sovereign AI and Confidential Computing As agents take on more autonomous, mission-critical tasks, the data they process becomes increasingly sensitive. Organizations deploying these advanced workloads require hardware-enforced protection and operational control that don’t sacrifice innovation. Whether safeguarding intellectual property during model training in the cloud or executing mission-critical workloads in fully air-gapped environments, Google Cloud and NVIDIA help provide verifiable security and local custody. Today, we are announcing new Sovereign AI capabilities for on-premises environments, alongside advancements in Confidential Computing for the public cloud: Sovereign AI on-premises with Google Distributed Cloud For mission-critical workloads that must remain or strictly isolated from the internet, Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) brings a managed cloud stack directly to your data center or edge facility. To advance sovereign AI initiatives, we are delivering new compute accelerators, multimodal models, and turnkey search capabilities across GDC air-gapped deployments: NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs on GDC: Following our preview announced earlier this year, the latest NVIDIA HGX B300 systems are now generally available (GA) on GDC. This brings industry-leading compute density and energy efficiency on-premises, providing the high-throughput platform foundation that demanding local inference workloads require. Gemini Flash models on GDC: We are expanding our sovereign model catalog with Gemini 3.5 Flash on GDC, accelerated by NVIDIA HGX B300. Organizations can now execute rapid, high-throughput multimodal reasoning, spanning text, audio, video, and imagery, entirely inside their air-gapped perimeter. Enterprise search capabilities on GDC: Available in preview, our enterprise search capabilities with Gemini on GDC air-gapped delivers an out-of-the-box conversational interface powered by multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). These capabilities are powered by Gemini on GDC air-gapped with NVIDIA HGX B300. Now, analysts and knowledge workers can instantly query, summarize, and cross-examine proprietary documents, media, and unstructured archives without custom engineering, keeping all indexing, embeddings, and interactions strictly within your sovereign security boundary. Beyond air-gapped on-premises deployments, you can also run sovereign AI workloads on NVIDIA AI infrastructure using Google Cloud Data Boundary to enforce controls such as regional data residency on our public cloud, or Google Cloud Dedicated for an isolated cloud run by a local independent partner such as S3NS in France or Thales in Germany. Confidential Computing in the public cloud As enterprise workloads scale, safeguarding highly sensitive intellectual property during active training, and user context and model IP during real-time inference is critical to maintaining a secure AI architecture. By combining Google Cloud’s advanced security runtimes with NVIDIA Confidential Computing, organizations can deploy high-performance generative AI models inside verified and trusted execution environments without sacrificing processing speed. G4 instances with Confidential Compute are GA: We are expanding access to privacy-preserving AI with Confidential G4 instances enabled by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. G4 Confidential GPUs, with NVIDIA Confidential Computing provide upgraded security without compromising on performance. Confidential Computing is available today on A4 instances enabled by NVIDIA HGX B200 and Intel TDX We are introducing Confidential Bare Metal to Google Cloud, recognizing the value of single-tenant bare-metal performance and isolation for frontier model AI serving. Our innovation leads to A4X Max instances (enabled by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 ) using NVIDIA Confidential Bare Metal . By extending hardware-rooted secure boot and attestation with encrypted DDR and NVLink interconnects, bare-metal AI workloads leverage this trusted execution boundary to protect user prompts and models during inference and training. The Google Cloud advantage Our co-engineering collaboration with NVIDIA integrates their full-stack accelerated computing platforms directly into AI Hypercomputer . This gives you the agent-native infrastructure you need to train, serve, and operate models at scale. Today's announcements deliver this unified foundation, combining the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform and high-throughput networking with expanded support for open models. Together, we also give you verifiable control over your data. With new sovereign AI deployments and confidential computing across NVIDIA infrastructure, you can protect your most sensitive workloads using hardware-enforced security and local data residency. Because we design hardware and software together as a single system, you can run models across different architectures without rewriting code. Your compute cycles stay focused on the workload, so you ship AI products faster. To get started with these new capabilities, please contact your Google Cloud sales representative.

title: Managed RAG search inside the sovereign perimeter: Gemini on GDC enterprise search
raw_text: National security agencies and other sovereign and highly regulated organizations handle incredibly sensitive data such as classified reports, field manuals, and sensitive multi-modal datasets. Search and multimodal intelligence that’s available in the public cloud can help teams manage and analyze that data, but due to strict data sovereignty mandates, that data cannot leave the customer premises. The alternative has been to deploy custom agentic search inside a secure, disconnected perimeter, but until now, that meant months building and maintaining custom infrastructure — stitching together models, building speech-to-text and optical character recognition (OCR) pipelines, configuring vector databases, and managing a bespoke user interface. Today, we're excited to announce enterprise search capabilities with Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) air-gapped accelerated by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to help solve the above challenges. In preview, this fully managed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) search experience runs entirely inside your physical security perimeter, with no connection to the public internet or to Google Cloud's global infrastructure. Your teams can now upload their files into a conversation and ask Gemini to find information about it, summarize it, compare it, or translate it. Every answer cites its sources, and conversations persist between sessions. Enterprise search capabilities on GDC enable your teams to search across siloed data and unlock powerful insights. With these capabilities, you can now: Go from hundreds of pages to a cited answer: Ask questions across long manuals, reports, and policies, and see exactly which files each answer came from. Work across languages: Ask in one language and get answers grounded in documents written in another, or have Gemini translate them. Ask one question across many formats: Combine audio recordings, video clips, images, and spreadsheets with no separate transcription or OCR steps. Pick up where you left off: Conversations and files persist between sessions, so you don’t have to start from scratch on long-running work. Keep access need-to-know: Each user's chats and files are private to that user, and access follows the identity provider groups you already manage. Users can work with PDF, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files, plus TXT, HTML, PNG and JPEG images, WAV audio, and MP4 video. Each file can be up to 100 MB, and each chat up to 500 MB. Core architectural layers: under the hood Let's follow a user query through each layer of the stack: signing in, ingesting files, generating the response with Gemini, and storing the session. Every step happens on the organization's air-gapped network. Identity and access Users sign in through their organization's identity provider. Administrators map the service's user role to identity provider groups, and only members of those groups can access the application. Each user's chats and uploaded files are private to that user. Document ingestion and embedding When a user uploads a file, it goes straight to the app's object storage bucket. The backend records the file's metadata in the app's managed PostgreSQL database, which is optimized for search. The backend then splits the file into chunks, such as groups of PDF pages or tiles of an image, and writes them to the bucket. A Gemini embedding model running natively within the GDC deployment converts each chunk into a vector, which the backend stores in the app's PostgreSQL database. When the user asks a question, the state-of-the-art (SOTA) Gemini model running entirely on GDC inside the customer’s data center first rewrites the question with context from the conversation. The backend then embeds the rewritten question with the same model and searches the vector database. Model serving The backend then combines the question, the conversation history, and the best-matching data into a single multimodal prompt and sends it to a Gemini endpoint running on NVIDIA HGX B300 systems in that same GDC deployment. Gemini is natively multimodal — it accepts text, images, audio, and video as input, so it can reason across data coming from different file types in a single context, and doesn't require separate speech-to-text and OCR models. The answer then streams back to the user with citations to the source files. Persistence Lastly, the persistence layer keeps each conversation's state. Each question and answer is stored in the system’s database and uploaded files stay in object storage, so users can reopen an earlier session and pick up where they left off. Built for classified and sovereign environments With Gemini and enterprise search on GDC, prompts, responses, uploaded documents, and embeddings never leave your organization's air-gapped network, and every model runs locally. Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 disk encryption using locally managed HSM keys, and in transit with TLS using FIPS-approved algorithms. Local IAM integration with granular role-based access control (RBAC) governs access to resources. GDC air-gapped has U.S. DoD IL6 accreditation and is designed to support strict requirements in alignment with FedRAMP High security controls. Code execution: Compliance and security To deliver precise, deterministic answers from structured spreadsheet data (such as CSV and XLSX files), Gemini enterprise search leverages the Gemini inference stack's local code-execution engine. When handling analytical queries — such as computing the average salary across departments — Gemini dynamically generates Python code and runs it securely within Agent Substrate , an open-source execution runtime built for large-scale agent orchestration. To mitigate security risks inherent to executing LLM-generated code, Agent Substrate enforces strict network isolation and runs workloads inside gVisor sandboxes , helping ensure strong isolation boundaries without sacrificing inference performance. Bringing frontier models to the sovereign data center You no longer have to choose between uncompromising security and cutting-edge multimodal intelligence. Enterprise search, Gemini 3.5 Flash and databases optimized for search run together inside the GDC air-gapped perimeter with no dependency on the internet to bring the best autonomous capabilities to the sovereign cloud. Explore the GDC air-gapped documentation and contact your GDC representative to learn how you can best leverage these search capabilities in your sovereign cloud.

title: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are now available in Google Antigravity
raw_text:
Whether you are iterating on a quick bug fix or planning a complex migration, different tasks call for different models. In keeping with Google Cloud's commitment to an open ecosystem and to give developers the right model for every job, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are now available in Google Antigravity for Google Cloud customers. Claude Opus 5.5 is built for complex work while Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a faster, lower-cost complement. Once enabled by an administrator, developers can select Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 directly from the model picker. Administrators can also select Google’s Gemini models, including Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 4 Argon. The models apply across Antigravity 2.0, Antigravity CLI and our recently released Antigravity IDE extensions for VS Code, JetBrains IntelliJ, and Visual Studio. This lets you choose the right model for the job, under a unified enterprise billing and security boundary. In this post, we’ll share two engineering patterns for building in Antigravity using these models. To view the entire list of models supported in Antigravity across subscriptions, see our documentation here . Multi-model engineering patterns in Antigravity Having multiple model families available inside the same agent harness unlocks practical multi-model workflows that improve code quality while controlling latency and cost. Pattern 1: Cross-model verification ("LLM-as-a-Judge") in loop and graph workflows When building agentic loops or multi-step graph workflows, using the same model to both write code and review its own output can reinforce model-specific blind spots. Pairing two distinct model families, one as the implementer and another as the validator (judge), provides independent verification before moving to the next stage of a workflow. In Antigravity, you can run this pattern either interactively or via automated subagents: Plan and implement with Model A: Start in planning mode using Claude Opus 5.5 or Gemini 4 Argon to design and implement a multi-file change. Validate with Model B: Before committing or advancing the loop, switch models, or invoke a one-shot /model check in the CLI, to have a different model family critique the implementation against your test suite and requirements. Pattern 2: Pairing reasoning models with Flash subagents Complex engineering tasks often combine a few high-reasoning decisions with dozens of high-volume, mechanical lookups (searching files, grepping logs, checking lint output, or classifying test failures). Running every lookup on a frontier model can increase both latency and spend. Antigravity's Subagent customization system ( .agents/agents/*.md ) lets you assign specific model tiers ( inherit , flash , or pro ) to specialized subagents. When your primary session is running a more powerful model. Subagents configured with model: inherit use your active session model for deep reasoning subtasks. Subagents configured with model: flash offload high-speed search, classification, and triage work to Gemini Flash models. For example, you can define a fast log-triage subagent in .agents/agents/test-triager.md : code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', '---
name: test-triager
description: Runs unit tests, classifies failures, and returns a concise summary of failing assertions.
model: flash
tools:
 - read
 - edit
---

Run the requested test targets, classify any failures by root cause (compilation error, assertion failure, or timeout), and return a structured summary to the parent agent.'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fbb9a66b050>)])]> And a cross-model code reviewer subagent in .agents/agents/gemini-judge.md : code_block <ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "---
name:cross-model-judge
description: Independent LLM-as-a-judge verifier that audits diffs and edge cases using Gemini Pro.
model: pro
tools:
 - read
---

Review the current workspace diff against the user's requirements. Check for regressions, missing edge-case tests, and security issues. Output a pass/fail verdict with specific line references."), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7fbb9b054650>)])]> With this setup, you can delegate rapid test-and-classify loops to test-triager and trigger cross-model-judge to validate the final diff, combining the strengths of each model in a single workflow. Getting started Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are available now for Google Cloud customers using Antigravity: Administrators (Gemini for business): Third-party partner models do not draw from the pooled Gemini Enterprise Standard and Plus edition monthly token quota. Instead, usage is billed on a pay-as-you-go basis through your existing Google Cloud Billing account, so overages must be enabled. Visit “Gemini Enterprise” > “Settings” > “AI developer tools” in the Google Cloud Console to configure overage billing, spend limits and authorize partner models for your organization. See Configure AI developer tools settings for step-by-step instructions. Administrators (Gemini platform): You can also enable partner models if you are using Antigravity through the API in Gemini platform. Enable Claude models in Model Garden and complete the standard Anthropic terms. Developers: Update to the latest version of Antigravity 2.0, the Antigravity CLI, or the Antigravity IDE extensions, and open the model picker (or run /model ) to select the right model for your task. To learn more about enterprise governance and multi-agent configuration, visit the Google Antigravity Enterprise documentation . You can switch the active model between turns in the same conversation thread while preserving workspace state, open artifacts, and terminal context. Note: Lightweight first-party Gemini models continue to run in the background to handle high-frequency client-side coordination, such as context management and summaries. They consume first-party tokens and can incur charges.
